name: Chroming Out
description: Describes the specific psychological state where a heavily augmented individual begins to experience their chrome as more instinctively 'natural' than their biological tissue — a perceptual inversion that aug-culture communities in Meridian 88 debate as either a sign of successful integration or early-stage dissociation disorder. The term was coined in the aug-modification parlors clustered around the Tier 2-3 border district called the Seam, where unlicensed chrome-workers serve clients who can't afford Corponation-certified augmentation clinics. It's distinct from full dissociation ('going porcelain'); chroming out is a temporary, often pleasurable state during peak aug-performance.
cultural_impact: The term has created a cultural split between aug-positive communities who use it as a compliment for seamless integration and medical professionals who use it as a clinical warning flag, leading to friction whenever aug-users interact with corporate healthcare systems.
key_figures: Chrome-worker and community advocate Jessamyn Oduya-Parrish
Neurologist Dr. Riku Halvorsen-Chandra (antagonistic clinical usage)
locations: Underbelly aug-parlor 'The Fitting Room', South Shelf
Tier 2 labor blocks near the Fabrication Yards
story_hooks: A Tier 2 factory worker who has been chroming out more frequently during grueling shifts starts to wonder if her employer's mandatory productivity implants are deliberately inducing the state to push her past safe working limits.

A Tier 4 corporate client visits an unlicensed Seam parlor specifically to experience chroming out, believing it will give them a competitive edge — and the chrome-worker must decide whether to serve them or refuse on ethical grounds.

An aug-positive rights organization wants to get 'chroming out' reclassified from a medical symptom to a protected psychological state — and they need a sympathetic test case to bring before the Meridian 88 Health Arbitration Board.
definition: The perceptual state where a heavily augmented person's chrome feels more instinctively responsive and 'natural' than their biological tissue; can be experienced as euphoric integration or, in excess, as early dissociation.
usage_example: 'After the third double shift, Kweku stopped noticing the weight of the arm entirely — he was fully chroming out, running on actuators without thinking about it once.'
spread: Common across Tier 1-3 aug communities; Tier 4-5 are aware of it but use clinical language instead; the term itself is considered too 'Seam-adjacent' for polite corporate conversation
